sentences.text: Owenodon is a member of the class Ornithischia and belongs to the family Iguanodontidae.
The genus contains the single known species O. hoggii, which serves as the type species for the group.
The only known fossil is a partial dentary, or lower jaw bone, found in the Purbeck Limestone dated to the middle Berriasian.
The fossil bone was damaged during initial preparation but was successfully freed from the surrounding rock matrix in 1975.
This specimen was presented to the Natural History Museum in London in December 1901 and assigned the catalogue number NHMUK PV R 2998.
Richard Owen first described the species in 1874, originally assigning it to Iguanodon as I. hoggii.
Peter Galton established the genus Owenodon in 2009, naming it after the original species description.
The evolutionary position of Owenodon within ornithopod evolution remains uncertain due to the limited fossil material available for study.
David Norman and Paul Barrett transferred the species to Camptosaurus in 2002, but Peter Galton later established the genus Owenodon for it in 2009.

Kenneth Carpenter and Yvonne Wilson challenged the placement of the species in Camptosaurus in 2008, arguing it was more similar to Camptosaurus dispar than to the newly described Camptosaurus aphanoecetes.
Greg Paul considered the species too incomplete to be placed in Camptosaurus and suggested it was an undiagnostic nomen dubium within Ornithopoda or Camptosauridae.
David Norman considered the separation of Owenodon into its own genus to be provisional, arguing the decision was based more on stratigraphy and geography than on anatomical differences.
Galton interpreted Owenodon as a more derived iguanodontid than Camptosaurus but less derived than Lurdusaurus.

Analyses by McDonald et al. from 2010 to 2017 found Owenodon to be an early member of Ankylopollexia, while Herne et al. (2019) found it further from Iguanodon than Camptosaurus, either unresolved between Ankylopollexia and Dryosauridae or closer to Ankylopollexia.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Owenodon as Dryomorpha.
Owenodon lived approximately 143 million years ago during the Berriasian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Europe.
The time range for Owenodon is recorded as Tithonian to Berriasian, from 149.2 to 137.05 million years ago.
The fossil was found in the Cherty Freshwater Beds of the middle Purbeck at Durlston Bay, dating to the middle Berriasian age within the Tirnovella occitana zone.
The type specimen of Owenodon was found in the Lulworth Formation of the Purbeck Limestone Group and dates to the middle Berriasian stage.
In 2012, Peter Galton expanded the geographic range of Owenodon by adding a tooth from the El Castellar Formation of Spain, while removing most Romanian material from the genus.
Owenodon hoggii is considered a taxon with inconsistent and uncertain classification.
